methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's cancellation of four NoVA data centers due to local backlash signals that even concentrated AI infrastructure faces resistance, potentially stalling both deep capability development and any spillover distribution effects to other regions.

signals.title: Appalachian author: Who pays when Virginia’s data centers go quiet or get sold to another firm?
signals.signal_reading: Questioning data center revenue permanence in Pittsylvania and Russell County exposes the shallow nature of infrastructure-only economic development—physical assets without local capability building leave rural regions vulnerable when corporate decisions shift elsewhere.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke's proactive coalition hiring outside expertise to develop an AI center plan signals intentional capability building beyond NoVA, suggesting potential for distributed deep learning if the initiative focuses on skills development rather than just infrastructure attraction.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A governor-ordered statewide AI cybersecurity plan centralizes defensive AI expertise at the state level, likely concentrating sophisticated capability in Richmond and NoVA government/contractor hubs rather than distributing threat response capacity across regions.

signals.title: Roanoke County Schools opens new career and technology center - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Opening a new career and technology center in Roanoke County creates infrastructure for distributed skill-building that could enable peer-to-peer AI fluency development, provided curriculum evolves beyond traditional tech training to include hands-on AI literacy.
